title: Periodic conditional measurements on a photonic chip
authors: Xuan Chen, Ruo-Yu Yin, Xiao-Wen Shang, Xi-Jun Yuan, Ze-Feng Lan, Hong-Jing Du, Yi-Jun Chang, Bao-Jing Liu, Wen-Hao Zhou, Xi Tan, Eli Barkai, Hao Tang, Xian-Min Jin
abstract: Quantum measurements not only extract information but also reshape quantum evolution through measurement backaction. Here, we investigate periodic conditional measurements, in which coherent evolution is repeatedly interrupted by local measurements. We show that the bright and dark modes of the conditional evolution operator provide a unified spectral description of both the post-selected final state along no-detection trajectories and the statistics of detection events. Using a three-dimensional photonic chip, we demonstrate on-demand state engineering through dark-mode preservation and bright-mode selection, enabling the protection of topological corner states and excited-state shelving. We further observe the predicted transition of the total detection probability on an effectively infinite one-dimensional lattice and identify its microscopic origin in Floquet near-dark modes. These results establish periodic conditional measurements as a general framework for engineering conditional quantum states and manipulating event-detection statistics in monitored quantum dynamics.
summary: The research explores periodic conditional measurements on a photonic chip, showing how repeated measurements can be used to engineer quantum states. By analyzing the spectral properties of the measurement operator, the authors demonstrate selective state preservation (dark modes) or steering toward the longest-lived component (bright modes). This establishes a general framework for controlling quantum dynamics through measurement backaction.
main_problem: The paper investigates how periodic conditional measurements reshape quantum evolution by repeatedly interrupting coherent evolution with local measurements.
main_result: They established that periodic conditional measurements provide a unified spectral description for both the post-selected final state and the statistics of detection events, enabling programmable state engineering.
method: The analysis uses the biorthogonal eigenbasis of the conditional evolution operator G to distinguish between decaying 'bright modes' and persistent 'dark modes'.
model_or_system: The experiment is performed on a scalable, layer-structured three-dimensional photonic chip using photonic waveguide arrays. The dynamics are modeled by the conditional evolution operator G = (1 - P)U(tau).
key_observables: Conditional final state (via dark/bright modes), first-detection probability distribution {F_n}, and total detection probability P_det.
important_parameters: The measurement period $\tau$ is a key tunable parameter, which controls the spectral properties and the transition between different dynamical regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the spectral decomposition of the conditional evolution operator G and compares results to the Quantum Zeno limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the measurement process, the physical chip setup, and plots showing the dependence of detection probability and spectral weights on the measurement period $\tau$.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical framework of periodic conditional measurements, then demonstrates state engineering using photonic chips (e.g., protecting topological states), and finally analyzes the transition of the total detection probability as a function of the measurement period $\tau$.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, platform-specific realization of controlling quantum dynamics via measurement backaction, which is central to understanding open quantum systems and quantum control.
